--- title: "Speech perception: discrimination" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_FON_PC_DISCRIMINA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_FON_PC_DISCRIMINA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Percepción del habla: discriminación*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_FON_PC_DISCRIMINA.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Speech perception: discrimination, from age 4 to 6 (2,196 administrations in 3 cohorts). AUC .39–.53 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2008 | | Battery | SERNICLAES | | Format | auditory stimuli | | Items | — | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | La tarea consiste en identificar si los dos sonidos que se oyen corresponden a la misma sílaba o a dos sílabas distintas. El evaluador o evaluadora marcará la respuesta del niño o la niña pulsando con el ratón sobre la casilla Misma o Diferentes. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework The **categorical perception** tasks (Serniclaes battery) use synthetic syllables ranging from BA to PA in voicing steps. In identification, the child says which syllable they hear; in discrimination, whether two syllables are the same or different. **Minimal pairs** ask the child to decide whether two real syllables are the same or different. They measure the precision of phonemic categories, the basis of letter–sound correspondences. **Phonological fluency** (saying, in 30 seconds, words that begin with a given phoneme) measures something else: lexical access from a sound and executive control. **What the evidence says:** - **Dyslexia shows a categorical perception deficit, clearer in discrimination.** A meta-analysis confirms the deficit compared with children of the same age and with younger readers at the same level. The effect is larger in discrimination than in identification [@noordenbos2015meta]. - **In Spanish, what fails is the boundary between categories.** In 204 Spanish children, those with dyslexia discriminated pairs that cross the phonemic boundary worse and some within-category differences better (allophonic perception) [@serniclaes2021allophonic]. That is why the total of correct responses mixes two effects of opposite sign. - **Its predictive value is modest and not entirely phonological.** In 237 children, perception at age 5½ predicted reading a year later without going through phonemic awareness. These tasks also capture decision making [@snowling2019speech]. In another study, its effect on decoding disappeared when phonological processing was controlled [@mcbridechang1997growth]. The evidence is therefore contradictory. - **Phonological fluency reflects access, not representations.** In 66 Greek children with dyslexia or developmental language disorder, word production was lower, but the size of clusters of related words was the same as in 83 controls [@mengisidou2019fluency]. **What our data show.** - **Categorical perception.** Discrimination does not predict persistent difficulty (AUC .39–.53) and identification barely does (.51–.63). This is to be expected if the total of correct responses is scored: the identification slope and between- and within-category discrimination should be computed from the item-by-item responses. - **Minimal pairs.** Low stability (ρ = .07–.39) and AUC from .45 to .69, better from age 5. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, .63–.66 at ages 6–7. - **Phonological fluency.** A single session at age 5 (793 children, almost all from Preleo schools): AUC of .68 against persistent difficulty and of .59–.62 against low comprehension. It is related to phonological awareness, letters and reading (ρ = .41–.43). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.2| 2012| 157|2016/17 | 386| 382| 0| 17| | 5.2| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 894| 0| 894| 35| | 6.2| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 916| 266| 650| 34| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.2| 382| 2012| 15.76| 4.74| 16.00| -0.27| 1.05| 0.26| | 6.2| 266| 2010| 18.54| 4.64| 18.50| 0.12| 0.00| 0.38| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 4.2| 382|0.8–25 |0–27 | | | 6.2| 266|11.7–28 |8–31 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.2, r = .09); Phonological awareness (5.2, r = .11); Phonological awareness (6.2, r = .16). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .39–.53. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .50–.54. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_PC_DISCRIMINA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .51–.58 (2 time points; 266–270 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|----:|---:|---:| | 4.2| 382| 2012| 10| 12| 12| 12| 16.0| 19| 22| | 5.2| 894| 2011| 12| 12| 12| 14| 18.0| 22| 24| | 6.2| 266| 2010| 12| 12| 13| 15| 18.5| 22| 25| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_PC_DISCRIMINA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 269| 0.072| 0.241| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 386| 0.080| 0.430| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 382| -0.077| 0.132| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 386| 0.075| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 893| -0.039| 0.249| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 891| -0.085| 0.210| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 887| 0.016| 0.633| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 894| 0.061| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 916| 0.053| 0.112| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 914| -0.145| 0.029| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 913| 0.003| 0.929| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 916| 0.052| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Speech perception: discrimination” (code 2008; SERNICLAES battery) assesses speech perception. Stimuli are presented auditorily and the child responds by selecting on the screen. The time limit is 300 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 4 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .50–.54. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
